steps.u: uploader.go talks to *s3.Client directly so its tests need LocalStack. Refactor so Uploader depends on a small interface and the tests can use a fake. No behaviour change.

steps.a: Only `PutObject` and `HeadObject` are used. I'll define a consumer-side `objectStore` interface in the upload package with just those two methods (Go's 'accept interfaces' idiom) instead of a broad wrapper around the whole SDK client; `*s3.Client` satisfies it implicitly, so callers don't change.

reference.summary: Refactored a Go uploader to depend on a narrow consumer-side interface with only the put and head object calls instead of the concrete S3 client, with a compile-time check, so tests use an in-memory fake instead of LocalStack.
